items.q: What should you remember about **Healthy self = agency + gratitude**?
items.a: **Happy people across life stages approach the** world feeling they can act (agency) and appreciate what is (gratitude); these are indicators, not affirmations.

items.q: What should you remember about **Structure before symptoms**?
items.a: **Diagnose architecture (unconscious, defenses, character,** self) before chasing surface behaviors; physical health parallels (structure/function) apply to psyche.

items.q: What should you remember about **Iceberg model**?
items.a: **Unconscious processes most thoughts, feelings, and** behaviors; conscious mind's job is awareness, choice, and integration — not total control.

items.q: What should you remember about **Defenses are tools**?
items.a: **Projection, displacement, humor/sarcasm, affiliate defenses can** protect or harm; understanding *which* defense runs *when* beats blanket "stop being defensive.".

items.q: What should you remember about **Generative drive is the north star**?
items.a: **Aggressive drive (assertion) and pleasure drive** (enjoyment) are necessary but insufficient; flourishing requires generative striving — create, learn, contribute.

items.q: What should you remember about **Confidence is state-dependent**?
items.a: **People can be confident in many domains yet** fragile in one; map the specific cupboard (unconscious pattern, narrative, defense) rather than relabeling identity as "not confident.".

items.q: What should you remember about **Salience is selective attention**?
items.a: **Thousands of stimuli compete; mental health includes** consciously placing attention on what matters instead of reactive fixation (especially negative internal dialogue).

items.q: What should you remember about **Overthinking ≠ thinking**?
items.a: **Rumination and procrastination often signal drive** imbalance or defense loops; restructure self-talk and examine which drive is starving.

items.q: What should you remember about **Envy vs generative living**?
items.a: **Biting sarcasm, destruction, and mass-violence narratives sit** at the pathological end of thwarted generative/aggressive balance; demoralization sits at the low-aggression pole.

items.q: What should you remember about **Spirited inquiry**?
items.a: **When answers aren't in one cupboard, search** many (childhood, defenses, drives, relationships, biology) before medicating or concluding; medicine supports exploration, doesn't replace it.

items.q: What should you remember about **Series roadmap**?
items.a: **Episodes 2–4 cover improvement protocols, relationships** ("magic bridge of the us"), and concrete tools; this episode is the assessment framework.
